source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public 13–15, 16:1–35 and 18 align directly. Public 16:36–50 maps to Hebrew 17:1–15; public 17:1–13 maps to Hebrew 17:16–28. All 214 original records, including every annotation, are hashed exactly. Later numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Supplies men as the missing object of took, flagged in a note; keeps Korah’s lineage and all Reubenite leaders, including On.
Retains the rebels’ holiness claim, every-one emphasis and accusation; too-far wording recurs in Moses’ reply.
Keeps tomorrow and election criterion; echoes verse 3’s accusation back to the Levites.
Retains accusation against the LORD rather than only leadership insubordination; hashes both complaint written/read forms.
Preserves their ironic description of Egypt as milk-and-honey land and accusation of self-appointed rule.
Keeps inheritance failure, harsh eye-gouging image and repeated refusal; notes figurative deception versus physical threat interpretations.
Retains anger, petition against offering and both denials; minchah left broad rather than assumed grain here.
Preserves severe divine threat and instant timing without deciding the community’s exact limits in the translation.
Retains title’s spirits/all-flesh language and challenge to collective punishment; no later philosophical anthropology imposed.
Keeps singular mishkan despite three names; does not rewrite as sanctuary or omit Korah to simplify geography.
Preserves specifically named households and vulnerable children rather than hiding them within an abstract group.
Preserves create/new wordplay, ground’s mouth, alive descent and Sheol without substituting a later hell doctrine.
Retains alive descent, closing earth and removal through death, not mere expulsion.
Retains source of fire and exact 250 deaths, distinct from the earth-swallowing event.
Makes holy referent the censers, not coals; keeps Eleazar distinct from Aaron and burned remains explicit. Hebrew 17:2.
Keeps self-ruin and holy status of censers despite offerers’ sin; passive hammering avoids inventing artisan identity. Hebrew 17:3.
Defines outsider by priestly ancestry, not ethnicity; leaves him’s referent open with note. Hebrew 17:5.
Preserves the accusation as community speech without inserting a narrator’s rebuttal. Hebrew 17:6.
Makes plural posture referents explicit and retains repeated threat of instant consumption. Hebrew 17:10.
Preserves 14,700 and explicit exclusion of earlier deaths from that count. Hebrew 17:14.
